name: Johnson Service Group PLC
executive_summary: Johnson Service Group PLC (JSG.L) is a UK and Ireland textile rental business (HORECA linen and Workwear) that the quantitative screen rates as a **strong buy** (7/22 models; composite 0.85; cheapness, quality, dividend and risk families all pass). The investment case rests on sustained margin expansion, a progressive dividend (4.8p FY25, +20%), disciplined capital returns (£90.3m buybacks since 2022), and valuation metrics that screen attractively (P/E 16.3, P/B 2.0, yield 3.2%, ROE 12.7%). FY25 preliminary results (RNS, 3 March 2026) show revenue up 4.3% to £535.4m and adjusted operating profit up 16.4% to £72.5m (margin 13.5%), with management targeting at least 14.0% in 2026. The key debate is whether headline cash-flow and cheapness metrics overstate underlying economics: the screen flags an FCF basis mismatch (filing/Yahoo ~£100.6m vs screen TTM ~£27.4m), while the company’s own FCF definition was £69.1m in FY25, and H1 2026 trading showed flat revenue with HORECA organic decline amid hospitality pressure.
investment_thesis:
For a value investor, JSG combines screen-level cheapness with operational quality that is visible in primary filings rather than inferred from multiples alone. Revenue has compounded from £513.4m (2024) to £535.4m (2025) while adjusted operating margin expanded 140bp to 13.5%; ROCE rose to 17.1% (2024: 15.5%). The business model—long-term rental contracts, high retention (Workwear 94%), and scale in a fragmented market—supports recurring cash generation: operating cash flow was £139.9m in FY25 (preliminary results). Dividend cover held at 2.5x on adjusted EPS, and the board returned £54.7m via buybacks in FY25 alone.

The quantitative screen alignment is strong: passes include Graham Enterprising, FCF Yield, Quality Value, Dividend Growth, Piotroski F-Score, Composite Value and Earnings Quality, with debt/equity at 62% and data quality 20/20. Cheapness is not purely statistical—adjusted diluted EPS grew 19.8% to 12.1p, and management remains on track for its 14% margin target despite macro headwinds. Capital allocation is shareholder-friendly (progressive dividend, repeated buybacks, accretive bolt-ons such as Empire Linen) while leverage (0.95x adjusted EBITDA at Dec-25) sits comfortably inside a 1.0–1.5x target and well below covenant limits (3.0x max). Main Market admission (August 2025) broadens the investor base without altering the core textile-services focus.
financial_review:
**Source coverage.** Primary analysis draws from RNS body extracts: FY25 preliminary results (3 March 2026), FY25 full-year trading update (16 January 2026), and H1 2026 trading update (10 July 2026). Companies House annual report bodies for FY24 and FY25 are present in the index but contain largely cover/highlights pages rather than full financial tables or principal-risk text. **No interim statutory accounts** (half-year report / 10-Q equivalent) are indexed (`interim`: 0); H1 2026 colour comes only from the July trading update. Historical 2022–2023 figures below use **Yahoo fallback** (`financials_annual.json`) where filing bodies lack detail.

**Annual trend (FY24 → FY25, preliminary results).**

| Metric | FY25 | FY24 | Change |
|--------|------|------|--------|
| Revenue | £535.4m | £513.4m | +4.3% |
| Organic revenue | +1.4% | — | — |
| Adjusted operating profit | £72.5m | £62.3m | +16.4% |
| Adj. operating margin | 13.5% | 12.1% | +140bp |
| Adjusted EBITDA | £166.8m | £152.6m | +9.3% |
| Statutory operating profit | £58.8m | £54.7m | +7.5% |
| Adjusted PBT | £64.5m | £54.8m | +17.7% |
| Statutory PBT | £50.8m | £47.2m | +7.6% |
| Adjusted diluted EPS | 12.1p | 10.1p | +19.8% |
| Statutory diluted EPS | 9.2p | 8.4p | +9.5% |
| Full-year dividend | 4.8p | 4.0p | +20.0% |

Segment FY25 (preliminary): HORECA revenue £389.8m, adj. operating profit £59.8m (margin 15.3%); Workwear revenue £145.6m, adj. operating profit £21.0m (margin 14.4%). Organic growth: HORECA +1.0%, Workwear +2.4%.

**Balance sheet and leverage (FY25, preliminary).** Net debt (including IFRS 16) £159.2m (Dec-24: £115.6m); bank debt £112.4m. Increase reflects £35.9m estate capex, £54.7m buybacks, and £17.4m dividends, partly offset by trading performance. Leverage (adj. EBITDA / net debt incl. IFRS 16) **0.95x** vs covenant maximum 3.0x; interest cover covenant minimum 4.0x with “significant headroom” per management. Committed RCF **£135.0m** matures August 2027; refinancing discussions underway. Shareholders’ equity £275.1m (Dec-24: £306.9m), reduced by buybacks. Defined benefit pension **surplus** £4.9m (IAS 19); triennial actuarial valuation (Sept-25) in progress; deficit recovery contributions ceased pending outcome.

**Cash flow (FY25, preliminary).** Operating cash flow £139.9m (2024: £141.8m). **Company-defined free cash flow** £69.1m (2024: £74.6m)—defined as OCF less textile rental item spend and capital element of leases. Textile rental item spend £65.8m; PPE capex £35.8m. Exceptional items £6.0m (Main Market listing £1.7m, reorganisation £3.4m including Lancaster closure, Bristol fire £0.4m, M&A £0.5m). **Yahoo fallback** reports FCF £100.6m and OCF £139.9m for 2025—the higher FCF figure likely reflects a narrower capex deduction and does not match the company’s stated £69.1m. The screen’s TTM FCF (~£27.4m) diverges further; treat FCF-yield-dependent metrics with caution until definitions are reconciled.

**Earlier years (Yahoo fallback only).** Revenue: £465.3m (2023), £385.7m (2022). Net income: £27.3m (2023), £29.0m (2022). These predate the full preliminary filing set and may reflect portfolio repositioning toward pure-play textile services; use for directional context only.

**Interim / trading update (H1 2026, 10 July 2026 RNS).** Revenue expected **£258.0m**, flat on H1 2025 (£257.5m). Organic revenue **(0.7%)**: HORECA **(2.0%)**, Workwear **+2.6%** (price-led). Net debt ~**£190.0m** at 30 June 2026 (Dec-25: £159.2m), reflecting dividend timing, £55.0m buyback programme (£17.3m returned by 9 July), working capital and capex; leverage described as towards the lower end of the 1.0–1.5x target. Management reiterates FY26 adjusted operating margin target of **at least 14.0%**; interim results due 8 September 2026. No indexed interim accounts body to verify H1 profit or cash flow.

**Going concern (preliminary results).** Directors adopted going concern through at least 30 June 2027, citing adequate liquidity, covenant headroom, and stress tests (adjusted operating profit would need to fall to ~75% of 2025 levels before facility headroom exhausted—a scenario deemed implausible).
risks_and_flags:
**Cyclical / end-market.** Hospitality weakness is the live issue: HORECA organic revenue fell 2.0% in H1 2026 after “significantly increased labour and premises costs” on end customers (preliminary results, H1 trading update). Market churn in independent hotels/restaurants is rising; price increases and renewals are “more challenging.” Shares fell sharply on the July 2026 update (news coverage). Seasonality may recover H2 volumes, but this is not yet evidenced in statutory interim accounts.

**Cost inflation.** Labour was 46.0% of revenue in FY25 (+140bp YoY); UK employer NI alone added ~£6.0m annualised impact, mitigated via pricing and efficiency. Energy remains 7.4% of revenue vs 6.2% in 2019 despite hedging (85–90% of 2026 usage fixed).

**Leverage and capital allocation.** Net debt rose £43.6m in FY25 and a further ~£31m to H1 2026, driven by buybacks, dividends and capex while leverage remains inside targets. Aggressive repurchases (£90.3m since 2022; new £55.0m programme May 2026) compress equity and raise financial risk if HORECA softens further. RCF refinancing due 2027—discussions started, terms not yet disclosed.

**Competitive / operational.** Fragmented textile rental market with price-led competition; customer attrition when service/price misaligned. Operational incidents: Bristol Workwear fire (June 2025, £0.4m exceptional; insurance claim pending), Lancaster site closure (£1.4m reorganisation). Goodwill £154.0m on £275.1m equity—no impairment in FY25 review, but acquisition integration risk persists.

**Accounting / metrics.** Heavy reliance on adjusted measures (FY25 exceptional £6.0m; amortisation £7.7m); statutory EPS 9.2p vs adjusted 12.1p. FCF definitions differ materially across company (£69.1m), Yahoo (£100.6m) and screen TTM (~£27.4m)—undermines confidence in FCF-yield screen passes without reconciliation. APM limitations explicitly acknowledged in filings.

**Pension.** IAS 19 surplus £4.9m is favourable, but triennial valuation (Sept-25) outstanding; medium-term objective remains liability buy-out.

**Governance.** Planned board succession (Lysanne Gray NED/Audit Chair from June 2026; CFO transition to Ryan Govender Oct 2025) appears orderly; no red flags in indexed filings.

**Regulatory / liquidity.** Going concern and covenants satisfactory per preliminary results; no qualified audit noted for 2024 statutory accounts. Negative working capital (£8.3m per Yahoo FY25) is typical for rental models but bears monitoring.

RiskTags: cyclical, competitive, leverage, pension, accounting, other
news_highlights:
Coverage over the past year is **moderate**: dominated by results, buybacks and governance, with limited independent strategic analysis.

**Results and strategy**
- “Johnson Service Group Reports 16% Profit Growth And Margin Expansion In FY25” (DirectorsTalk Interviews, 3 March 2026) — aligns with preliminary RNS.
- “Johnson Service Group H2 Earnings Call Highlights” (Yahoo Finance, 6 March 2026) — management cited price increases, lower energy costs and efficiency driving margin progress.
- “Johnson Service boosted by hospitality-facing segment” (Investors’ Chronicle, 3 March 2026) vs “Johnson Service shares plunge despite in-line results” (Sharecast.com, 3 March 2026) — market reaction mixed despite in-line FY25.

**Capital returns**
- Completion of £25.0m buyback at avg 141.05p (RNS, 8 January 2026); total buybacks since 2022 £90.3m.
- “AGM Statement & Launch of Share Buyback Programme” (LSE, 6 May 2026) — new £55.0m programme.
- Ongoing buyback transaction RNS through August 2026; TipRanks/Kalkine coverage of repurchases at 150–153p (July–August 2026).

**Trading / market reaction**
- H1 2026 trading update (10 July 2026): “Johnson Service Group Shares Slump Over 12% as Hospitality Weakness Hits First-Half Trading” (AskTraders, 10 July 2026); “Johnson Service backs outlook despite hospitality weakness” (Proactive Investors, 10 July 2026).

**Corporate / ownership**
- Main Market admission (August 2025) per preliminary results.
- NED appointment and Audit Committee/SID changes (RNS, 3 March 2026).
- “Tweedy, Browne Company LLC's Voting Stake… Climbs to 12.02%” (Kalkine Media, 29 July 2026).
- “Berenberg nudges up target price” (Sharecast.com, 19 January 2026).
- Institutional ownership ~80% (Yahoo Finance, 14–15 February 2026).

No material M&A beyond bolt-on contract acquisitions (£4.9m annualised revenue) or regulatory enforcement actions surfaced in the manifest. **Gap:** thin sell-side and trade-press depth relative to RNS volume; H1 2026 interim accounts not yet released.
research_rationale: Deep research largely confirms the screen’s quality-and-yield case—FY25 margin and dividend progress, covenant headroom, and Workwear resilience support accumulation—but FCF definition divergence, rising net debt from buybacks, and H1 2026 HORECA softness warrant a measured overlay rather than unqualified endorsement of the strong-buy signal.
